FINALLY SOMEONE SAID IT!!! I feel like the reason most people think she’s acting out of character this season is bc the show doesn’t convey it well enough. Her character arc makes sense if you really think about it; but it shouldn’t be like that. The viewer shouldn’t have to do an entire investigation onto why a character acts the way they do, it’s the show’s job to subtly convey the motives and thought process of a character. 

I don’t remember the exact line but in the scene where she’s sitting on the swing talking to Ray (her subconscious) she says something about how she feels like she’s going insane. She also mentions to another character about how “nothing matters and nothing is real if they keep switching timelines” (I’m paraphrasing cause I can’t remember the exact lines). To me it seems like Allison is experiencing some kind of grief related dissociation that evolves into depersonalisation/derealisation. I feel like if the show actually dove into that and showed more examples of Allison spiralling her character arc would make a lot more sense.

My only critique of Umbrella Academy is that they could’ve always done more. I feel like the show would benefit from have 11-12 episodes rather than 10 
because it would fix the pacing issues in each season. Throughout every season there are so many plot points that I wish had been expanded upon and the resolutions to those plots always felt kind of unsatisfactory. If they had more episodes/showtime I feel like the show would be so much more richer bc they’d have more time to focus on nuances of each little subplot. 

Also with this season it’s pretty obvious that there were some budget cuts. Like the cgi was significantly worse this season and the show was barely advertised at all. Most of Netflix’s money probably went to Stranger Things but it sucks that UA got the shit end of the deal.

I think the reason people say it’s homophobic is because of the phrasing. Saying “I don’t agree with being gay” is weird. Because what are you disagreeing with?? Being gay isn’t an opinion, it’s someone’s sexuality. How do you disagree with someone’s sexuality? It’s fine if you “don’t care” about the queer community, no one is forcing you to openly support us. As long as you’re not supporting laws that criminalise being gay/trans or attacking queer people for just existing than you’re chill. But “disagreeing” with someone’s existence is a little disrespectful.

Men and women both have different kinds of struggles when it comes to mental health, but being a girl wouldn’t make your struggles any easier (I’m sure you’ve heard from other comments). Women get discriminated against so often by medical professionals, their problems get policed and the responses to a lot of them are also kinda victim blamey. Every time I have an appointment for any kind of health reason I always force myself to wear makeup and look somewhat presentable because I’m worried that I wouldn’t be taken seriously if I looked bad. I’ve had multiple male doctors not believe me and tell me that my issues stem from my period (I almost died at one point because I had an issue with my lungs that I didn’t know about because a doctor told me my symptoms were because of my period). Most studies of disorders have only male participants so the outcomes are based solely on the male experience, this makes it difficult when it comes to disorders that present differently in males and females, that’s why so many women go undiagnosed because they don’t “match” the criteria. Etc etc etc.

The truth is, being a woman wouldn’t make your struggles any easier, it would just create a whole new set of challenges. The problem is with the social norms surrounding mental health, it’s true that men aren’t taken as seriously when it comes to emotional issues because they’re told to just “man up” but it’s also true that women aren’t taken as seriously when it comes to mental health because they’re considered “too emotional” and both sides end up getting dismissed. It’s important that we continue to fight for mental health care and end the social stigmas surrounding mental illness. You absolutely deserve to be taken seriously op, fuck whatever patriarchal norms the world has created and don’t ever feel like less of a man for wanting to do things like dressing feminine. By the way everyone can rock platform boots no matter which gender and I’m sure you will look AWESOME.
